page.layout: One page of running text in a single column; margin notes in the right margin: "Magistratus pericula." beside the first lines, and a group of notes beside the lower lines. Printed page number 213 at the top right; running head at the top centre; signature at the foot.

main_text.l: Tu ergo nunciterum vide, Annon perhoc
Iefuitarum decretum omnium Europaeorum
Regum & quorumcunq; Magistratuum Poli-
ticorum mors & vita ab arbitrio Iefuitici horo-
scopo suspendatur? Vt si hic illis dextrè
ascendat, ipsi viuant & valeant, sin minus, pereant?
Qua de re prædicta Venerorum calamitas, Re-
gis Britanniæ perpetua pericula, & illorum o-
mnium metus, qui hunc Ordinem sibi infestū
sentiunt, abundè testantur. Venetorum tamen
exemplum præcipuè confpicuum est, quòd
Respub. illa, vt dixi, Romano-Catholicam re-
ligionem hactenus, tanquam Imperii sui Palla-
dium, accuratè obseruet & acerrimè tueatur.
Quæ exempla quoties expendo, toties
exhorresco, cùm vid£ am quàm facilè sub præsen-
ti rerum statu inter nos simile quiddam in al-
terutram partem accidere possit, postquam in-
primis Gentis Iefuiticæ ad huiusmodi aliquem
effectum tam pertinaces & feruidi conatus ab
aliquot iam annis inter nos deprehenduntur.
Sed heic fortassis dicere voles, Inter nos ni-
hil ab hac parte esse periculi, quòd Iefuitis cum
Rege nostro probè conueniat, &c. Mallem te
dicere posse, Regi nostro cum Regni ordinibus
& his cum regia Maiestate probè conuenire.
Hoc enim ad Reipub. salutem aliquanto vti-
lius, & ad securitatem nostram firmius & effi-
cacius esset. Nunc autem hoc ab ste verè dici
agnosco, neq; tamen hoc ipsum follicitudinis meæ
caussam tollit, sed eandem potiùs auget.
{i} Magistratus pericula.

marginalia.note: Regis vita & fortunæ ab hac pendet, de Regni fortunis Iefuitarum affectus obnoxia.

page.notes: Right-margin notes are printed in small italic type and run together across lines; the notes beside the lower lines are partly obscured and read with doubt. The marginal note "Regis vita & fortunæ ab hac pendet..." is a best reading. "Venerorum" (first line) is uncertain and may be "Venetorum". "vid£ am" and "dicere voles" are doubtful print. The line "Cacius esset" is printed "cacius esset". The cut-off at the foot of the lower lines (line ends "effi-" / "cacius") is read as printed. The word "aliquanto" is clearly printed. The outlined middle-foot mark is not a numbered note.
